lives_lived.description: Has been having a rough day. Then again, a rough day is par for the course for you.

looped.description: Trapped in some form of time loop. When will it end? Who knows? Nobody.

wont_forget_eggs.description: Won't forget the eggs. Whatever that means.

entered_doppelganger.description: Seems to have some capacity to inhabit Doppelgangers.

was_nude.description: Enjoys a little time in the buff.

evil_player.name: Voice In Your Head
evil_player.description: The unwanted second voice in your skull: observant, insolent, and rather more frightened than he admits.

lives_lived.description: He's taken residence in your head with zero intention of leaving.

good_joke.description: Is fond of a good joke, even if at his own expense.

was_dreaming.description: Has the uncanny ability to identify when you're in a dream state.

baby.name: Baby
baby.description: A borrowed shape worn badly by something that remembers you.

baby_twice.description: Seems to be a monster baby, maybe.

doppelganger.name: Doppelganger
doppelganger.description: A body assembled from the lives the bell refused to let continue.

lives_lived.description: Is tied somehow to your time loop nightmare.

doppelganger_once.description: Can be inhabited if the situation allows it.

baby_once.description: Has been known to masquerade as a French child of questionable origin.

harold.name: Harold the Haggard
harold.description: Keeper of the tournament rolls, servant of the bell, and a bureaucrat exhausted beyond ordinary time.

lives_lived.description: Appreciates contestants showing up with proper equipment.

was_nude.description: He's seen some things. Most of them being you in the buff.

read_black_ledger.description: Has maintained the same impossible tournament ledger for longer than any person should remember.

shady.name: Shady the Relicmonger
shady.description: Tourney rival, dealer in questionable holiness, and owner of one excellent doublet.

lives_lived.description: Won't stand up and is just imitating.

shady_stabbed_twice.description: Has killed you often enough that neither of you can pretend it was an accident.

shady_truce.description: Remembers flashes of other lives and wants the chance to meet someone waiting in tomorrow.

announcer.name: Amy the Announcer
announcer.description: Town crier, reluctant conspirator, and owner of the loudest indoor voice in three counties.

heard_thirteenth_bell.description: Hears every bell, including the ones the rest of town forgets.

amy_trust.description: Has announced your death often enough to take it personally.

gamedev.name: The Redactor
gamedev.description: A custodian in the margins of the day. Knows the rules, dislikes the author, and edits with a heavy hand.

lives_lived.description: Dispenses wisdom with a smug competence.

system_reboots.description: Can strike entire variations from the record, though the bell appears to outrank him.

lives_lived.description: Lover? I hardly even know her. Boom.

fought_dream_monster.description: Sustains itself on ill-conceived combat encounters.

guard.name: Gilbert the Guard
guard.description: A tower guard trying very hard to survive until supper.

gilbert_spared.description: Can be defeated by paperwork, pity, or an aggressively unclothed contestant.

little_you.name: Little You
little_you.description: Left behind when you inhabit the face in the sky.

lives_lived.description: Could help set you up for success.

eggs_laid.name: Impossible Eggs
eggs_laid.description: A warm egg marked with tomorrow's date. The chicken refuses to explain.

was_chicken.name: The Crowned Chicken
was_chicken.description: For one brief and glorious life, the coop recognized your sovereignty.

entered_doppelganger.name: Echoes Inhabited
entered_doppelganger.description: Your abandoned selves are not strangers. With focus, you can cross the distance between you.

fought_dream_monster.name: Dreams Defied
fought_dream_monster.description: The nightmare can be hurt, but not with anything as simple as violence.

wont_forget_eggs.name: Mother's Warning
wont_forget_eggs.description: Do not forget the eggs. More specifically: do not forget what is written on them.

times_abducted.name: Echo Captures
times_abducted.description: The pale echoes collect you instead of killing you. That distinction feels important.

system_reboots.name: Days Redacted
system_reboots.description: You watched the bell erase an afternoon while it was still happening.

020a__eat_breakfast.title: Get some breakfast
dialog: Let's get some breakfast before we start chores.

030a__start_chores.title: No time for breakfast, gotta start work.
dialog: No time for breakfast, gotta start work.
I'll just take some bread with me to snack on.

010b__wakeup_repeat.speaker: player
dialog: Heavy storm two mornings in a row. Strange. Or a

020a__eat_breakfast.title: Let's get some breakfast before starting chores
dialog: Let's get some breakfast before we start chores.

030a__start_chores.title: No time for breakfast, gotta start work.
dialog: No time for breakfast, gotta start work.
I'll just take some bread with me to snack on.

050a__skip_day.title: Skip today until we've skipped 5 times.
dialog: How many times are we going to do this?
Whelp, guess it's time to start work

030a__start_chores.speaker: player
dialog: This sucks, you should stop working
I don't think that bread is so good...
010a__wakeup.title: Eat Moldy Bread

030a__start_chores.title: Keep Working
dialog: I need to silence the voice and keep working.

040a__process_restart.comment: This blank room redirects us to some other blank rooms to convert regular items into aged items
040a__process_restart.speaker: player

041a__process_aged_bread.comment: This blank room turns regular bread into moldy bread
041a__process_aged_bread.speaker: player

050a__skip_day.comment: Skip today until we've skipped 5 times.

050b__skip_day__stop.speaker: player
dialog: You can't skip anymore. We're restarting the day now.

1000__RESTART.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Death is not darkness. It is a room made from the instant before waking.]
It was not intended to be.
[[EMOTE]][Beyond the room, pale silhouettes repeat your final movements.]
Lives that did not make it back cleanly.
I know that they look like us.
I know they are getting closer.

1012__START.title: Return to morning with what you learned.

1160__FOURTH_WALL.title: Demand an audience with whoever maintains the loop.
dialog: I want to speak with them.

1020__FAKE_WORLD.comment: During your walk, you see a hazy form floating in the sky.
1020__FAKE_WORLD.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You leave the farm before the rain can decide whether to fall.]
The road has declined to participate.
[[EMOTE]][A flock hangs above the wheat field, each bird fixed in precisely the same wingbeat.]
It has begun forgetting the difficult parts.
[[EMOTE]][One bird turns its head. Beneath the feathers is a small human face—yours.]
I was happier when we were discussing breakfast.

1140__FAKE_WORLD.title: Answer the face with your own name.

1130__BAD_DREAM.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You strike the faceless dream. Your fist passes through and returns holding a wedding ring.]
Violence appears to be making the metaphor stronger.

1150__FAKE_WORLD.title: Let the borrowed memory carry you onward.
dialog: I feel like I've been here before...

1120__BAD_DREAM.title: Ask the dream whose memory this is.
dialog: Show me whose memory this is.

1120__BAD_DREAM.comment: Have a small dream sequence. What's that one doing awake? Take care of it.
1120__BAD_DREAM.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The dream opens into every home you might have known.]
Because tomorrow is written on the shells.
That is considerably more useful than the usual maternal shouting.
[[EMOTE]][The homes close one by one until only the sound of the bell remains.]

1110__EASTER_EGG_ENDING.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You step beneath the frozen flock. The world stutters.]
[[EMOTE]][Rain rises from the earth. Footprints close behind you. The sun jerks east.]
[[EMOTE]][A red sentence burns across the sky: UNAUTHORIZED VARIATION.]
What happens at the end of the correction?
[[EMOTE]][For the first time, the Redactor hesitates.]
[[EMOTE]][The field folds backward into your bedroom.]

1100__ABDUCTION.comment: Wake up scene to doppelgangers, shadowy figures.
1100__ABDUCTION.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You wake bound beneath the bell tower. Pale figures stand around a door drawn in red chalk.]
They seem to be saving us for something.
[[EMOTE]][The chalk door has no hinges, yet something knocks from the other side.]
[[EMOTE]][The chapel bell tolls. Every pale face turns toward you at once.]
And now the bell takes you back.

1090__TOURNEY.comment: You don't attend event (and event likely only existed in your head)
1090__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You search for your old tournament pennant. The cloth crumbles at your touch.]
That is not one year of dust.
The date stitched here is eighty-seven years old.
Perhaps memory is not proof of when something happened.
[[EMOTE]][Inside the pennant, dozens of names have been sewn over one another. Every name is yours.]
The tournament is part of it.
Then let us dream somewhere less pointy.

1080__INVESTIGATE.comment: The crying turns to wailing. It's getting louder. Turns to roaring.
1080__INVESTIGATE.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You bar the door and pretend the crying belongs to someone else's conscience.]
[[EMOTE]][The crying stops. Three careful knocks sound from inside the pantry.]
We do not keep a baby in there.
We barely keep flour in there.
[[EMOTE]][The pantry door opens. A pale figure wearing your height and none of your warmth steps out.]
Do not lie to the breakfast demon.
[[EMOTE]][More pale hands reach from the pantry than the pantry could possibly contain.]

1075__TOURNEY.comment: Leads to 1071 (registration) but with additional flavor.
1075__TOURNEY.speaker: player

1071__TOURNEY.title: Proceed as though this were intentional.

1170__ENDGAME.title: Abandon the tournament and climb the watchtower.

1074__TOURNEY.comment: An archery accident gone bad kills you. (roving)
1074__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Amy opens the sealed proclamation. Her smile falters.]
[[EMOTE]][Archers in the gallery turn their bows toward you with empty, synchronized faces.]
[[EMOTE]][The first arrow pins your shadow to the earth. The second finds the body attached.]

1073__TOURNEY.comment: An archery accident gone bad kills you. (butts)
1073__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][At the distance range, every target bears a crude painting of your face.]
Favorite to die in an educational manner.
Why do the targets look like me?
They looked like me before you arrived.
[[EMOTE]][The painted faces turn toward you. Shady's confidence disappears.]
[[EMOTE]][A target releases an arrow of its own.]
For the record, it was an excellent shot.

1072__TOURNEY.comment: You attend the archery tourney with all required equipment. Pick your competition.
1072__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: Results are entered in the permanent record.
[[EMOTE]][He offers a contestant's chip stamped with a tiny thirteen-spoked wheel.]
This grants access to the contestants' enclosure.

1073__TOURNEY.title: Enter the distance range and study the targets.
dialog: I want time to study the targets.

1074__TOURNEY.title: Enter the moving-target event.
dialog: If today is changing, I want to see it move.

1071__TOURNEY.comment: You attend the archery tourney but brought a sword
1071__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Harold's black ledger writes before his quill touches it.]
Why have you entered an archery tournament without a bow?
We may each keep one mystery.

1000__RESTART.title: Retreat and remember the breathing ledger.
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You retreat behind the registration tent, where the ledger whispers your name through the canvas.]
Next time, we bring the bow.
[[EMOTE]][A pale archer steps from the alley holding the bow you forgot.]

1070__TOURNEY.comment: You attend the archery tourney but forgot your clothes
1070__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You reach registration armed, determined, and entirely unclothed.]
Little Jon has returned in his ceremonial skin!
Object to the name after we solve the larger textile emergency.
At home, supporting my earlier decisions.
The ledger has a box for this.

1000__RESTART.title: [Retreat with what remains of your dignity.]
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You retreat behind the registration tent while Harold opens the ledger.]
We leave, dress, and return with a plan.
A sentence containing three things we have never successfully done.
[[EMOTE]][The alley darkens. A pale figure steps out wearing tournament garb cut precisely to your measurements.]
[[EMOTE]][The echo closes the distance. Morning follows.]

1060__INVESTIGATE.comment: The thing you're investigating turns out to be a doppelganger.
1060__INVESTIGATE.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You follow the cry to a cradle set neatly in the mud. No footprints approach it.]
[[EMOTE]][The child smiles with the exhausted recognition of an old friend.]
[[EMOTE]][Its small shape lengthens. Swaddling becomes burial cloth; fingers become pale jointed hands.]
You always come when we cry.
[[EMOTE]][The echo folds itself around you. The field goes dark.]

1056__CHICKEN.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You drive the pigs toward the acorn wood. The wolves do not hunt; they herd.]
They are steering us toward town.
[[EMOTE]][Each wolf wears a narrow strip of black ledger paper around its neck.]
[[EMOTE]][The pack closes the circle. Far away, Harold begins reading.]
The animals are part of the reset.
[[EMOTE]][The wolves leap as one. The last thing you hear is the bell.]

1055__CHICKEN.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The goats have climbed onto one another to avoid touching the rain.]
[[EMOTE]][From the top, you can see wolves gathering at the forest edge in a perfect circle.]
Those wolves are waiting for the bell.
Then let us be elsewhere when it rings.

1054__CHICKEN.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The flock accepts you. By dusk, you have a straw crown, three loyal hens, and no remaining human responsibilities.]
I have finally found my calling.
You have been poultry for six hours.
[[EMOTE]][At sunset every chicken turns toward the chapel. The thirteenth stroke sounds.]
[[EMOTE]][The crowned hen closes her eyes. The coop, the farm, and your glorious reign fold into morning.]

1053__CHICKEN.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The crowned hen presents a warm egg. Scratched into its shell is tomorrow's date.]
That date does not exist yet.
Neither does your dignity, but here we are.
[[EMOTE]][A hairline crack circles the egg like a bell's rim.]
Or tomorrow is trapped in the egg.
You are naked in a chicken court.

1052__CHICKEN.speaker: player
dialog: If she will not speak to a man, perhaps she will speak to a chicken.
That sentence contains several unearned assumptions.
[[EMOTE]][You remove your clothes and fashion a comb from a red stocking.]
I wish to observe the full catastrophe.
[[EMOTE]][The flock goes silent. The crowned hen inclines her head.]

1053__CHICKEN.title: Accept the crowned hen's impossible gift.

1051__CHICKEN.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The hens part around one black bird perched upon a tiny crown of straw.]
Her Majesty has better posture than you.
[[EMOTE]][The crowned hen pecks thirteen times, then points her beak toward the chapel.]
That something is wrong with today.

1040__INVESTIGATE.title: Investigate the disappearances.
dialog: Mysteriously disappearing in the dead of night.
No one knows where they're going.

1050__CHICKEN.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The farmyard waits beneath the rain: goats complaining, pigs plotting, chickens pretending innocence.]
Heroism is mostly feeding creatures that would eat you if they were larger.
[[EMOTE]][A hen taps the same three-beat pattern against her nesting box.]
She is doing that on purpose.

1055__CHICKEN.title: Inspect the tower of goats.
dialog: The goats could use a milking.

1056__CHICKEN.title: Take the pigs to the acorn wood.
dialog: When did the pigs eat last?

1051__CHICKEN.title: Find out why Ma warned you about the eggs.

1040__INVESTIGATE.comment: It's a normal morning. You hear a child crying. You don't have children.
1040__INVESTIGATE.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][As you coax the hearth awake, a child begins crying beyond the eastern field.]
That is either a baby or a very ambitious kettle.
Babies do not cry in languages.
[[EMOTE]][The cry repeats exactly—same breath, same hitch, same distant echo.]
Everything repeats if you are sufficiently cursed.
A child is alone in wolf country.
And our bacon is alone in pan country.

1060__INVESTIGATE.title: Follow the repeating cry.
dialog: What's a child doing out this way, anyways?
We should probably check it out.
Wouldn't want the wolves getting to it first.

1080__INVESTIGATE.title: Bar the door and stay with the hearth.
dialog: Not my child, not my problem.

1036__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][While stowing your bow, you trip and fall on your sword. The world fades to black.]

1035__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: Ah yes, good ol' Mister Stabs.
[[EMOTE]][While fumbling for your sword, you fall over your bow and black out.]

1034__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: Oh yeah, I've had this nightmare before.
Not forgetting my clothes this time.
Do you make a habit of showing up places in the buff?

1033__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: Glad I restrung it last night.

1032__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: Ah yes, good ol' Mister Stabs.
Bane of fingers and toes everywhere.

1030__TOURNEY.comment: Today's the fair. You remember the archery tourney. You remember you're a participant.
1030__TOURNEY.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][A tournament pennant snaps against your window.]
You say that with the confidence of a champion.
The goat was disqualified after judging.
[[EMOTE]][The chapel bell rings once. Your bowstring hums in answer.]
This time I am going prepared.

1013__START.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Thunder. Rain. The bell waiting at the edge of the same morning.]

1012__START.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You wake to the same thunder, in the same bed, beneath the same leaking corner.]
And yet your hair remains a disaster.
[[EMOTE]][The revellers outside repeat the same joke. The same woman laughs on the same breath.]
[[EMOTE]][The chapel bell rings once. Something in your ribs answers.]
The trick is finding which ones can bleed.

1020__FAKE_WORLD.title: Follow the road where the rain behaves incorrectly.
dialog: I want to see how far the mistake goes.

1030__TOURNEY.title: Investigate the tournament and its records.
dialog: The tournament keeps appearing in my memories.

1040__INVESTIGATE.title: Light the hearth and listen for the cry.
dialog: Then we follow whatever cries first.

1050__CHICKEN.title: Find the egg Ma warned you about.
dialog: Ma said not to forget the eggs.
For once, we listen to Ma.

1200__MARKET.title: Follow the impossible bell into town.
dialog: Every road bends toward the fair.
Let us meet the people waiting there.

1300__BELL_HEIST.title: I know what today is. Gather the others.

1010__START.comment: You jolt awake. There's a lot going on. A fair is in town.
1010__START.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You wake to thunder arriving half a heartbeat before the lightning.]
That is not how thunder works.
[[EMOTE]][Rain scratches the shutters. Beneath it, the chapel bell rings once.]
I promised Ma I would finish the chores before the tourney.
You also promised to stop drinking cider from the ceremonial ladle.
[[EMOTE]][Outside, revellers slog toward town through the same merciless rain.]
A whole day ahead of us.
Try not to die in it.

1140__FAKE_WORLD.comment: You deliberately form a memory-bridge with the abandoned lives.
1140__FAKE_WORLD.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The little face beneath the feathers opens its mouth.]
[[EMOTE]][The bird speaks every name you have worn in lives you cannot quite remember.]
[[EMOTE]][You press a hand to your chest and answer with the only truth all those names share.]
[[EMOTE]][Something on the far side remembers back.]
[[EMOTE]][The field remains beneath your feet, but another horizon opens inside your memory: the village seen through a vast pale face in the sky.]
[[EMOTE]][Within the shared memory stands another you—the first life that learned to answer.]
How many of us are here?
Every life the bell began again.
[[EMOTE]][Their memories gather into one exhausted figure—not a stranger, but a crowd forced to wear a single shape.]
Try not to make them regret it.

1141__FAKE_WORLD.speaker: player
dialog: I am not here to replace you.
Then help me stop the morning.
[[EMOTE]][The doppelganger grips the edges of your borrowed thoughts.]
You still believe you are the original.
[[EMOTE]][It forces you out of the shared body. You fall upward into darkness.]

1142__FAKE_WORLD.speaker: player
dialog: The ones who feared what came through the door.
[[EMOTE]][The bell rings. The answer is torn away before you can hear it.]

1141__FAKE_WORLD.title: Promise that no life will be discarded again.

1142__FAKE_WORLD.title: Ask what the bell has taken from them.

1171__ENDGAME.title: Use the crowned flock's thirteen-beat answer.
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You tap the thirteen-beat pattern taught by the crowned hen against the shared memory.]
Our finest diplomatic achievement remains becoming poultry.
[[EMOTE]][The doppelganger answers with the same pattern. The bridge steadies.]

1172__ENDGAME.title: Demand the truth from the echo.

1150__FAKE_WORLD.comment: You wake up from the dream (but are really still in a different dream) and there's a monster.
1150__FAKE_WORLD.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You wake in a different bed beneath a summer sky. Someone sleeps beside you without a face.]
I do not know this person.
You loved them in a life the bell did not choose.
[[EMOTE]][The faceless sleeper reaches for you with familiar tenderness.]
The dream would prefer we stayed.

1130__BAD_DREAM.title: Confront the borrowed memory.
dialog: If this life remembers me, I owe it an answer.

1040__INVESTIGATE.title: Reject this life and wake in the rain.

1160__FOURTH_WALL.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The room stops pretending to be a room. Red annotations appear in the air.]
I maintain the margins between one version of today and the next.
Because the bell divides a life.
You have become inconveniently good at catching it.
A voice made from everything you refuse to say aloud.
Break the mechanism and tomorrow resumes.
The mechanism was built to contain you.
[[EMOTE]][A red line strikes through the room. Morning shows beneath it.]
Try to make the next death informative.

1170__ENDGAME.comment: You reproduce the memory-bridge from the western watchtower.
1170__ENDGAME.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You leave the tournament line and climb the western watchtower.]
We are abandoning a perfectly survivable plan.
No plan involving this day is survivable.
[[EMOTE]][Gilbert looks at your lack of clothing, then toward the heavens for patience.]
I am not trained for this.
[[EMOTE]][You slip past while professional dignity prevents pursuit.]
[[EMOTE]][From the tower, the impossible face in the sky is unmistakable: yours, assembled from clouds and old grief.]
[[EMOTE]][You nock an arrow and draw until the bowstring hums at the same pitch as the chapel bell.]
The bridge answered to memory before.
This time we give it a note to follow.
That is either inspired or fatal.
[[EMOTE]][You speak the names the frozen bird remembered. The bowstring carries them into the sky.]
[[EMOTE]][The echo answers. For one impossible instant, archer and abandoned lives share the same memory.]
[[EMOTE]][Inside the echo, the doppelganger turns toward you.]

1171__ENDGAME.comment: The shared memory reveals the allies required to confront the bell.
1171__ENDGAME.speaker: player
dialog: A promise from the one who wakes.
The bell keeps every abandoned life inside this shape.
At sunset it chooses one of us to begin again.
The black book names the chosen life.
The crier remembers the forbidden stroke.
The rival dreams of the tomorrow we lost.
Make a rule the bell has never heard.
[[EMOTE]][The thirteenth stroke begins. The memory-bridge fractures into a thousand dawns.]
[[EMOTE]][The shared sky collapses into a single black page.]

1172__ENDGAME.comment: You say some cool catch phrase. You begin monologuing. You're distracted, though, and get captured.
1172__ENDGAME.speaker: player
dialog: Because you keep refusing to hear it.
[[EMOTE]][The doppelganger presses a thumb to your borrowed forehead.]
Return when you can name all the lives you abandoned.
[[EMOTE]][The bell strips you from the shared body.]

1200__MARKET.comment: Enter the fair and discover that its bells do not agree with time.
1200__MARKET.speaker: player
dialog: Where honest folk exchange honest coin for dishonest pies.
You say that like you've been.
Some of them have eaten bad pies.
[[EMOTE]][Canvas stalls crowd the muddy square. Ribbons snap overhead. A fiddler is losing a public argument with a goose.]
And good morrow to Amy's indoor voice.
His Lordship welcomes you to the Feast of Saint Bartholomew!
Did that bell just ring thirteen?

1210__MARKET_CRIER.title: Ask Amy about the thirteenth bell.

1230__MARKET_TOWER.title: Go straight to the bell tower.

1210__MARKET_CRIER.comment: Amy denies the impossible bell until the player proves the day repeats.
1210__MARKET_CRIER.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You shoulder through the crowd toward Amy's little red platform.]
The next archery registration begins at—
[[EMOTE]][Amy lowers her proclamation. Her smile stays public. Her eyes do not.]
If anyone asks, we never spoke.
That is a very normal response.

1211__MARKET_CRIER.title: Tell her you're not leaving.
dialog: I would like to know why.

1211__MARKET_CRIER.comment: The player first learns that Amy also hears the impossible bell.
1211__MARKET_CRIER.speaker: announcer
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Amy drags you behind the platform and pins you between two barrels of commemorative turnips.]
Every fair day, the bell rings once too many.
By supper, it feels like a dream.
At sunset, I am handed a final proclamation.
[[EMOTE]][A shadow passes over the barrels. It has your face.]

1000__RESTART.title: [Try to remember her warning.]
dialog: Next time, tell me what tomorrow's proclamation says.
[[EMOTE]][The turnip barrels explode inward. The world follows.]

1213__MARKET_CRIER.comment: On a later loop, Amy trusts the player and points them to Harold's records.
1213__MARKET_CRIER.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Amy pulls you behind the turnip barrels.]
Harold keeps the contestants ledger beneath the registration tent.
Every name you have ever used is in it.
And if Harold offers you a contestants chip—
You truly have done this before.

1220__MARKET_SHADY.comment: Shady sells fake relics and reveals that he remembers fragments of other loops.
1220__MARKET_SHADY.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Shady has established a stall beneath a banner reading CERTIFIED HOLINESS.]
A square of cloth sneezed upon by Saint Cuthbert.
Did Saint Cuthbert have a cold?
I hate that this is working on me.
[[EMOTE]][Shady leans close. His salesman's grin slips.]
I dreamt you drowned in a washbasin.
Then a goat crowned you king.
To be fair, we were asking for at least one of those.

1222__MARKET_SHADY.title: Tell him the dreams are memories.

1221__MARKET_SHADY.comment: A comic relic purchase goes predictably badly.
1221__MARKET_SHADY.speaker: player
dialog: And a solemn vow not to wash it.
Our finances are now managed by a haunted radish.
[[EMOTE]][You press the cloth reverently to your face.]
[[EMOTE]][You collapse into a basket of devotional onions.]

1222__MARKET_SHADY.comment: The player forms an uneasy alliance with Shady.
1222__MARKET_SHADY.speaker: player
dialog: Let's not poison a promising friendship with lies.
[[EMOTE]][The chapel bell groans above the market.]
Every time it rings, I taste iron.
And I remember your face burning in the sky.
After sundown he carries a black ledger to the bell tower.
Gilbert hit me with a halberd.
If you find a way into that tower, fetch me.

1000__RESTART.title: Leave before he sells you something.
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Behind Shady, a reliquary sneezes. Everything goes dark.]

1230__MARKET_TOWER.comment: The player scouts the tower and meets Gilbert properly.
1230__MARKET_TOWER.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The bell tower rises behind the chapel, old stone stitched with fresh iron.]
Nothing says harmless village bell like six new locks.
Not while I was wearing trousers.
Do you guard a screaming ledger?
[[EMOTE]][From inside the tower comes a muffled chorus of your own voice.]
Many things sound like many things.

1232__MARKET_TOWER.title: Make a heroic dash for the door.

1240__LEDGER.title: Amy sent me for Harold's ledger.

1231__MARKET_TOWER.comment: Kindness earns Gilbert's future cooperation, but not survival.
1231__MARKET_TOWER.speaker: player
dialog: At sunset, Harold climbs the tower.
He reads from the black book.
Then I wake in my bed with blood on my boots.
Also, Harold says if the bell is not rung, tomorrow comes.
He does not say it like it is good.
[[EMOTE]][The tower door shudders. Something heavy tests its hinges from within.]
[[EMOTE]][The door bursts open. A dozen pale hands pull Gilbert backward.]
Tell my pension I loved her!

1232__MARKET_TOWER.comment: An attempted tower rush ends in a historically accurate amount of halberd.
1232__MARKET_TOWER.speaker: player
dialog: You cannot stop a determined heart!
I can stop the rest of you.

1240__LEDGER.comment: Break into Harold's records tent in search of the black ledger.
1240__LEDGER.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You circle behind the registration tent as Amy begins an unusually loud proclamation.]
A PIG OF UNCOMMON GIRTH HAS ESCAPED!
[[EMOTE]][A large pig barrels through the square wearing Shady's relic banner.]
[[EMOTE]][Beneath Harold's desk, a black leather book breathes softly.]

1241__LEDGER.comment: The ledger reveals the loop is a ritual built around the player.
1241__LEDGER.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Every page bears a date, a name, and a manner of death.]
[[EMOTE]][The ink crawls across the parchment as you read.]
At the thirteenth stroke, all unresolved lives return to first light.
I was hoping there was another charming parasite.
[[EMOTE]][A sketch shows a human figure split down the middle. Both halves have your face.]
It's made from the lives I leave behind.
Because the page beneath your hand says it knows we're reading.
[[EMOTE]][The ledger screams in fifty-seven versions of your voice.]

1000__RESTART.title: [Remember what the bell contains.]
dialog: You were not meant to read that.
[[EMOTE]][Harold closes the ledger. You are still inside it.]

1242__LEDGER.comment: Waiting for Harold provides a more personal piece of the conspiracy.
1242__LEDGER.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You wedge yourself into a cabinet labeled DISQUALIFICATIONS: MORAL.]
[[EMOTE]][Harold enters and drops his public smile with the tent flap.]
Fifty-eight thousand, two hundred and nine.
He has done this fifty-eight thousand times.
And still files it by hand.
Because the first tomorrow was worse.
[[EMOTE]][Harold stamps your forehead with a red DISQUALIFIED seal.]

1241__LEDGER.title: Grab the ledger anyway.
dialog: Then I should read my own file.
[[EMOTE]][You seize the breathing book from Harold's desk.]

1000__RESTART.title: Ask him to explain the first tomorrow.
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The red seal burns through your thoughts.]

1300__BELL_HEIST.comment: The player begins the true-ending campaign after recruiting allies across loops.
1300__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You enter the fair with the confidence of someone who has already died in every available direction.]
Then we ring the bell backward.
You say that like dying is a minor scheduling conflict.

1310__BELL_HEIST.comment: Amy joins the conspiracy and clears the square.
1310__BELL_HEIST.speaker: announcer
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Amy spots you before you reach her platform.]
[[EMOTE]][Amy climbs her platform and unfurls a blank proclamation.]
A ROYAL TAX ASSESSOR HAS ENTERED THE EAST GATE!

1320__BELL_HEIST.comment: Shady joins the bell heist for reasons both noble and sartorial.
1320__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Shady is packing false relics into a very real reliquary.]
We're breaking into the bell tower.
I also promise every relic is authentic.
The bell is why you remember dying.
[[EMOTE]][Shady looks toward the tower. For once, he has no joke ready.]
In one dream, I had a daughter.
I should like the chance to meet her.
[[EMOTE]][He produces a roll of lockpicks, two knives, and a small devotional onion.]

1330__BELL_HEIST.title: Confront Harold before he reaches the tower.

1330__BELL_HEIST.comment: Harold explains his role and the original catastrophe.
1330__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You find Harold in the registration tent, black ledger chained to his wrist.]
You have broken into my tent in fifty-three distinct ways.
The answer is no to all of them.
Then you know enough to be dangerous.
Tell us about the first tomorrow.
The court alchemists built a door beneath the tower.
A door into every life you might have lived.
The king wanted an army that could not die.
Kings do love a dreadful idea in expensive trousers.
You were ordered to open it.
Every possible you stepped through at once.
So you trapped the day before.
I believe I was a coward.

1331__BELL_HEIST.title: Ask Harold to help end it.

1331__BELL_HEIST.comment: The player recruits Harold by offering him accountability instead of absolution.
1331__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: And if tomorrow destroys the kingdom again?
Also, the kingdom is mostly livestock and people selling fake thumbs.
You do not need to be forgiven.
You need to open the tower.
[[EMOTE]][Harold studies each of you. The bell tolls nine.]
At the thirteenth stroke, it names the life to be preserved.
If the names are read backward before the final stroke—
Or every abandoned life returns at once.
[[EMOTE]][Harold unchains the ledger from his wrist.]
I will get you through the lower door.
After that, the tower will defend itself.

1332__BELL_HEIST.comment: Violence against Harold proves the ledger is a jealous employer.
1332__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Shady cuts the chain at Harold's wrist.]
[[EMOTE]][A parchment tongue wraps around Shady's arm.]
[[EMOTE]][The ledger swallows Shady, doublet and all.]

1340__BELL_HEIST.comment: The assembled party reaches Gilbert at the tower.
1340__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The four of you cross the empty square. Gilbert lowers his halberd.]
You told me never to stand aside.
Do you have the revision in writing?
Gilbert, if we succeed, you may not have a pension.

1341__BELL_HEIST.title: Remind Gilbert that he trusted you before.

1342__BELL_HEIST.title: Let Amy issue a lawful order.

1341__BELL_HEIST.comment: Remembered compassion earns a bloodless passage.
1341__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: You told me about the blood on your boots.
You told me you were afraid.
I have never spoken to you.
You declared love for your pension.
You also tried to save me.
[[EMOTE]][Gilbert looks at the tower door. Something behind it scratches his name into the wood.]
If there is supper tomorrow, I favor stew.
[[EMOTE]][Gilbert raises his halberd and unlocks the door.]

1342__BELL_HEIST.comment: Amy defeats Gilbert through the awesome force of fabricated procedure.
1342__BELL_HEIST.speaker: announcer
dialog: By authority of the Office of Bells, Fairs, and Lesser Geese, stand aside.
Are you refusing a direct order under Poultry Addendum Seven?
I have not read Addendum Seven.
She's killing him without a blade.
Your pension is forfeit pending a three-year review.
[[EMOTE]][Gilbert unlocks the door with furious efficiency.]

1350__BELL_HEIST.title: Enter before he checks the statutes.

1350__BELL_HEIST.comment: The party climbs through discarded lives toward the bell.
1350__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The tower is larger inside. Stairs coil upward through impossible dark.]
Do not let them touch you.
They want to be the life that continues.
[[EMOTE]][Little You turns and fires into the crowd of echoes. A path opens.]
[[EMOTE]][The bell tolls eleven. The whole tower shudders.]
Do not correct the professional counter.

1360__BELL_HEIST.comment: At the bell, the player chooses how to confront the divided self.
1360__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You burst into the bell chamber beneath a sky wearing your face.]
[[EMOTE]][Harold opens the book. Pages whip backward in the wind.]
[[EMOTE]][The bell draws breath for its twelfth stroke.]
There is something in the bell.
[[EMOTE]][The doppelganger unfolds from the bronze, built from every death you abandoned.]
Rules are what remain when people do not.

1362__BELL_HEIST.title: Let the Voice read the final name.

1361__BELL_HEIST.comment: Brute force breaks the bell but not the loop.
1361__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Together you swing the iron clapper into the bell's rim.]
[[EMOTE]][Bronze splits. The sky splits with it.]
[[EMOTE]][Every abandoned life pours through the crack at once.]

1362__BELL_HEIST.comment: The player gives the Voice agency and learns its origin.
1362__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: The ledger calls you the voice within.
Maybe you're the part that remembers who we were.
Or the part that makes jokes during fatal injuries.
[[EMOTE]][You place the ledger beneath your hand. The Voice speaks through your mouth.]
Life that stayed to close it.

1363__BELL_HEIST.comment: The player refuses the ritual's false choice and names every abandoned life.
1363__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Around you, the abandoned selves stop fighting.]

1370__BELL_HEIST.comment: The Thirteenth Bell campaign resolves and rejoins the epilogue.
1370__BELL_HEIST.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The bell rings backward through eleven, ten, nine—each stroke returning a stolen possibility.]
[[EMOTE]][The doppelganger stands at the edge of the vortex, no longer monstrous. Merely tired.]
[[EMOTE]][The doppelganger steps into you like a reflection returning to glass.]
You've been waiting all day to say that.
[[EMOTE]][The final backward stroke sounds. Somewhere beyond the tower, a rooster crows for a morning that has never happened.]

2000__START.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The world folds inward, carrying every remembered life with it.]
Then you made a choice the rules could not predict.
[[EMOTE]][The thunder stops. For the first time, nothing resets.]
What happens to me when we leave the loop?

2003__EPILOGUE.title: You're part of me. Come on.

2004__EPILOGUE.title: Maybe we both deserve some quiet.
dialog: Maybe we both deserve some quiet.

2003__EPILOGUE.comment: The player accepts the voice and walks into tomorrow.
2003__EPILOGUE.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Somewhere beyond the vortex, morning birds begin to sing.]
Those had better be normal birds.
Only one way to find out.

2004__EPILOGUE.comment: The player releases the voice and walks into tomorrow alone.
2004__EPILOGUE.speaker: player
dialog: Try not to die before breakfast.
[[EMOTE]][The voice fades. Somewhere beyond the vortex, morning birds begin to sing.]

2005__EPILOGUE.speaker: player
dialog: And, against every reasonable expectation, you made it to tomorrow.

2001__RESTART.speaker: player
dialog: This time, we know the way out.
And at least twelve ways not to go.

2002__RESTART.speaker: player
dialog: Not like I'd forget the eggs twice in a row.

1020R__REVISIT.comment: Return to the road after learning how the false sky behaves.
1020R__REVISIT.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You return to the dry road beneath impossible rain.]
We can skip the surprised part.

1110__EASTER_EGG_ENDING.title: Force the day to reveal its correction.

1030R__REVISIT.comment: Return to the tournament with prior knowledge.
1030R__REVISIT.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You arrive before Harold can pretend not to recognize you.]
Whichever one your ledger wrote first.

1031__TOURNEY.title: Prepare for the tournament without repeating old mistakes.

1090__TOURNEY.title: Examine the records instead of competing.

1040R__REVISIT.comment: Return to the repeating cry with prior knowledge.
1040R__REVISIT.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The child cries beyond the eastern field on precisely the expected breath.]

1060__INVESTIGATE.title: Meet the echo in the field again.

1080__INVESTIGATE.title: Wait for the echo to come inside.

1050R__REVISIT.comment: Return to the farm after its impossible discoveries.
1050R__REVISIT.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The crowned hen is already waiting beside tomorrow's nesting box.]
We know where the strange parts are.

1055__CHICKEN.title: Check the goat tower and the waiting wolves.

1056__CHICKEN.title: Follow the ledger-marked pack into the wood.

1200R__REVISIT.comment: Return to the fair after hearing the impossible bell.
1200R__REVISIT.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][The fair repeats its muddy pageant. You no longer wait for the thirteenth stroke to know it is coming.]
Then we speak only to whoever still has something to teach us.

1210__MARKET_CRIER.title: Find Amy behind the proclamation platform.

1220__MARKET_SHADY.title: Find Shady beneath the false-relic banner.

1230__MARKET_TOWER.title: Return to Gilbert and the locked tower.

1240__LEDGER.title: Go directly to Harold's black ledger.

1300R__REVISIT.comment: Resume a failed bell heist without replaying its setup.
1300R__REVISIT.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][You enter the fair already counting backward from thirteen.]

1333__HAROLD_REVISIT.comment: Return to Harold's decision during a repeated heist.
1333__HAROLD_REVISIT.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Harold waits in the registration tent with the ledger chained to his wrist.]
You know what happens if I open the tower.
I also know what happens if you do not.

1331__BELL_HEIST.title: Ask Harold to choose tomorrow again.

1364__BELL_CHAMBER_REVISIT.comment: Return directly to the bell chamber after a failed final choice.
1364__BELL_CHAMBER_REVISIT.speaker: player
dialog: [[EMOTE]][Memory carries you past the locks, the stairs, and the gathered echoes to the choice that killed you last.]
We have heard the old rule.
Let us try a better answer.

1362__BELL_HEIST.title: Let the Voice read the divided name.
